_readme: Single source of truth for venue DATA. Consumed by:
- scripts/fetch-events.js  — `aliases` are merged into venue-name normalization
- scripts/manage-wp-pages.js — seeds /venues/{slug}/ pages (page.*)
- wordpress/comedy-houston.php — fetches this file from GitHub raw for
JSON-LD venue addresses and for linking event-card venue names to venue pages
PAGE COPY OWNERSHIP — read this before editing page.description_html.
Venue pages are CREATE-ONLY. The `page.*` fields below seed a venue page
the first time it is published; after that WORDPRESS IS THE SOURCE OF
TRUTH, so body copy, links and images are edited in the WP editor and the
sync will not touch them. Expect the copy here to drift from the live page,
and do not treat it as a mirror. To deliberately push copy from here over a
live page, run the Manage WordPress Pages workflow with that slug in its
`overwrite` input.
The non-page fields are still live config and DO take effect on every run
of anything that reads them: `aliases`, `address`, `phone`, `website`,
`same_as`, `schema_type`. LocalBusiness schema is only emitted for venues
with a street address, so TODO-address venues degrade gracefully. Note the
schema is written at page-create time, so correcting an address here does
not update an already-published page's JSON-LD without an `overwrite` run.
`page.enabled` is NOT just a sync switch — the plugin reads it to decide
whether event-card venue names link to /venues/{slug}/. Setting it false
stops syncing AND unlinks the venue sitewide (the page is never deleted).
SEO caveat: the site runs Rank Math, but the plugin makes the synced
_ch_meta_title / _ch_meta_description post meta win over it (see
filter_seo_plugin_title in comedy-houston.php). On a page that has been
synced, editing the SEO title or description in Rank Math's UI will have
no visible effect — change page.meta_title / page.meta_description here
and re-run with `overwrite` instead.

page.title: Houston Improv — Shows, Tickets & Info
page.meta_title: Houston Improv Comedy Club — Shows, Tickets & Info | Comedy Houston
page.meta_description: Houston Improv at the Marq*E on the Katy Freeway: national headliners, two-item minimum, free parking, tickets sold by the table. Every upcoming show, price, and ticket link, updated daily.
page.description_html:
The Houston Improv is the city's big room for national headliners, tucked into the Marq*E entertainment center at 7620 Katy Fwy, on the Katy Freeway just west of the 610 Loop. It is Houston's stop on the Improv circuit, the chain that has set the template for the American comedy club since Budd Friedman opened the original in New York in 1963, and it books like it: multi-night weekend runs from comics you already know off Netflix specials, late night TV, and the big podcasts.

The room holds around 450 at tables, dinner theater style, with a curtain that pulls back to shrink the space for smaller bills. That layout is the one thing worth understanding before you book, because tickets here are sold as complete tables unless a listing says otherwise. A pair buying two seats may end up sharing a table with strangers, and a group of six can claim a table outright by buying the whole thing. It is a different transaction from most clubs, and it rewards deciding your party size before you check out.

Houston Improv vs. Punch Line vs. the small rooms: which one tonight?

If the goal is seeing a name you already recognize, the Improv is usually the answer, and the calendar below will show you why. Punch Line Houston, downtown at GreenStreet, is the other room booking that tier of touring comic, and the practical difference is how you sit: Punch Line is general admission, first come first served, so getting there early is what buys you a good seat, while the Improv sells you the table itself. One rewards punctuality, the other rewards planning.

Then there is the other half of Houston comedy. The Den and The Riot are the small rooms, where tickets cost less than parking downtown and the lineups are the city's best working comics rather than television names. Those rooms are not competing with the Improv so much as covering the night the Improv does not: no minimum, no table math, no headliner premium.

Worth knowing if the headliner price gives you pause: the Improv's own weeknight local showcases run at a fraction of a weekend ticket, usually in the low teens against thirty or forty dollars for a touring act. Same room, same stage, same free parking, a good deal less money. They show up on the calendar below alongside everything else.

Food, drinks, and the two-item minimum

Every guest owes a two-item minimum, and the club counts it generously: any food item or beverage, with or without alcohol, counts toward it. A soda and an appetizer settles it. There is a full kitchen and table service through the show, so plan to eat during rather than before if that suits you.

Parking is complimentary behind the venue and across the Marq*E lot, which quietly does more for the price of the night than it sounds like. Add a downtown garage to a comparable ticket elsewhere and the Improv often comes out even.

Know before you go

  • Where: 7620 Katy Fwy Ste 455, Houston, TX 77024, inside the Marq*E entertainment center on the Katy Freeway.
  • Age: 18 and up to get in, 21 and up to drink. Bring a photo ID, they check.
  • Minimum: two items per person. Food or drink, alcoholic or not, both count.
  • Seating: tickets are sold as complete tables unless the listing says otherwise.
  • Parking: free, behind the club and throughout the Marq*E lot. Full breakdown in our Houston comedy club parking guide.
  • Box office: Monday to Wednesday 10am to 5pm, Thursday 10am to 8pm, Friday and Saturday 10am to 10pm, Sunday noon to 8pm.
  • Show nights: Wednesday through Sunday, with early and late shows on headliner weekends.
  • Tickets: sold through Ticketmaster and the club box office. Headliner weekends sell out, so book ahead rather than at the door.
  • Follow the club: improvtx.com/houston and @improvhouston.

Every show at the Houston Improv appears in the listings below automatically, updated twice a day, alongside every other comedy show in Houston. If it is on sale, it is here.

page.title: Punch Line Houston — Shows, Tickets & Info
page.meta_title: Punch Line Comedy Club Houston — Shows, Tickets & Info | Comedy Houston
page.meta_description: Punch Line Houston, downtown at GreenStreet: national headliners, Spanish-language nights, 18+, two-drink minimum, general admission seating. Every show, price, and ticket link, updated daily.
page.description_html:
Punch Line Houston is the downtown stand-up room at 1204 Caroline St, inside the GreenStreet complex, in the space that used to be the House of Blues restaurant and now runs as a club with its own entrance. It seats about 250, which makes it the middle size in Houston comedy: better funded and better booked than the neighborhood rooms, small enough that the back row still feels close to the stage.

The club opened downtown in September 2024 as the fourth Punch Line, a name that traces back to the original San Francisco room and its run as a proving ground for touring comics since 1978. Under head of comedy operations Amanda Kyser it books more than 350 shows a year and puts Houston comics on the bill ahead of the touring headliners, which is rarer at this size than it ought to be. If you have watched a local open mic and wondered where those comics go next, a fair number of them go here.

Punch Line vs. Houston Improv vs. the small rooms: which one tonight?

Punch Line and the Houston Improv are the two rooms in the city booking national touring comics week in and week out, and choosing between them is mostly logistics. Punch Line is downtown, general admission, and first come first served, so arriving early is what gets you a good seat. The Improv is out on the Katy Freeway with free parking and sells tickets as whole tables. Downtown means a garage or valet here; the Katy Freeway means a free lot there. Factor that in and the ticket prices sit closer together than they look.

For a cheaper and smaller night, The Den and The Riot run rooms where the lineups are Houston's best working comics rather than names off television, at a fraction of the ticket. Punch Line sits deliberately between the two: touring headliners most weekends, local showcases and one-off series on the weeknights.

Comedia en Español and the local bills

Punch Line programs Spanish-language stand-up more consistently than any other large room in Houston. Look for the shows marked en Español on the calendar below, where touring Spanish-language comics play the same stage as the English bills rather than getting pushed to an off night. Every one of them is also collected on our Spanish comedy in Houston page if that is what you came for.

Food, drinks, and the two-drink minimum

There is a two beverage minimum per guest in the showroom, and the club counts non-alcoholic drinks toward it: mocktails, sodas, and juices all satisfy the requirement, so it is not a tax on not drinking. The kitchen runs a full menu with table service through the show.

Standard downtown club rules otherwise: no outside food or drink, and bags larger than 10 by 10 inches, backpacks, and professional cameras stay in the car.

Know before you go

  • Where: 1204 Caroline St, Houston, TX 77002, inside GreenStreet downtown.
  • Age: 18 and up, unless you are with a parent or legal guardian. Photo ID required.
  • Minimum: two beverages per guest in the showroom. Non-alcoholic drinks count.
  • Seating: general admission, first come first served. The club cannot hold or reserve specific seats, so groups should arrive at least 45 minutes early and walk in together.
  • Doors: one hour before showtime, except late shows. The box office opens an hour before the first show, on show days only.
  • Parking: valet on site, or the GreenStreet garage on Clay between Main and Fannin, which connects by skybridge. Full breakdown in our Houston comedy club parking guide.
  • Show nights: Tuesday through Sunday most weeks, with the touring headliners on Friday and Saturday.
  • Tickets: sold through Ticketmaster. Every upcoming date is listed below with prices and direct links.
  • Follow the club: punchlinehtx.com and @punchlinehouston.

Every show at Punch Line Houston appears in the listings below automatically, updated twice a day, alongside every other comedy show in Houston. If it is on sale, it is here.

page.title: The Secret Group — Shows, Tickets & Info
page.meta_title: The Secret Group — Comedy Shows, Tickets & Info | Comedy Houston
page.meta_description: The Secret Group in EaDo: comedy almost every night, most tickets under $10, no drink minimum, and more open mics than anywhere in Houston. Every show, price, and ticket link, updated daily.
page.description_html:
The Secret Group is an independent comedy venue and bar at 2101 Polk St in EaDo, on the corner of Polk and St. Emanuel, and it is the engine room of Houston's alternative comedy scene. There are two stages under one roof: the main showroom, and a smaller room called The Box with its own marked entrance on Polk. Between them there is stand-up on the calendar essentially every night of the week, which is not true of any other room in the city.

What makes it matter is the volume and the price. A typical week here runs open mics, weekly series with names like $2 Bill and Master Debaters, late-night dirty shows, headliner showcases, and touring alt-comedy and podcast acts passing through. A lot of it costs under ten dollars and a good deal of it is free. This is where Houston comics build hours, and where an audience can watch the scene actually happen rather than watch a finished product.

The Secret Group vs. the big clubs: which one for which night?

The Houston Improv and Punch Line sell you a known quantity: a touring headliner, a two-item or two-drink minimum, and a ticket priced accordingly. The Secret Group sells the opposite. You will often not recognize a single name on the bill, the ticket is under ten dollars, and there is no minimum at all, so the whole night can cost less than parking downtown.

The other practical difference is that the big clubs run on a weekend rhythm. If it is a Monday or a Tuesday and you want to see live stand-up, The Secret Group and The Riot are realistically your two options. For an audience willing to gamble on unfamiliar names, that is a feature: weeknight rooms are where comics try the material that is not ready yet.

Open mics, and going up yourself

The Secret Group hosts more open mics than anywhere else in Houston, one most nights of the week, and they are listed on our Houston open mic page with sign-up details. If you are trying stand-up for the first time, this is the most likely place in the city for it to happen. If you are just watching, an open mic is free and unpredictable in roughly equal measure.

Food, drinks, and no drink minimum

There is a full bar and, in the club's own words, no drink minimum of any kind, which is unusual for a comedy room and is a real part of why a night here stays cheap. Non-alcoholic options include locally roasted Cruiser cold brew on a nitro tap.

The venue does not have a kitchen, and rather than pretend otherwise it lets you bring food in from outside. EaDo has plenty within a short walk, and eating before or during the show is entirely normal here. One rule worth knowing: photos and video are not allowed during comedy sets.

Know before you go

  • Where: 2101 Polk St #A, Houston, TX 77003, in EaDo. The club entrance is at the corner of Polk and St. Emanuel; The Box has its own entrance on Polk.
  • Age: comedy shows starting before 10pm are 18 and up, shows starting after 10pm are 21 and up. Concerts are generally all ages. Check the individual event.
  • Minimum: none. No drink minimum, which is rare for a comedy club.
  • Food: no kitchen, but outside food is welcome inside the venue.
  • Parking: street parking on the surrounding blocks, metered in places but free after 6pm, plus pay lots nearby usually running $10 to $20. Rideshare is often easier. Full breakdown in our Houston comedy club parking guide.
  • Dress code: none.
  • Tickets: sold through Eventbrite. There is no staffed box office, so most shows can also be bought at the door on the day, though anything likely to sell out is safer online.
  • Hours: 5pm to 2am daily.
  • Follow the club: thesecretgrouphtx.com and @secretgrouphtx.

The Secret Group also runs music, karaoke and other non-comedy nights. Those are filtered out of the list below, which is comedy only, updated twice a day, alongside every other comedy show in Houston.

page.title: The Riot Comedy Club — Shows, Tickets & Info
page.meta_title: The Riot Comedy Club — Shows, Tickets & Info | Comedy Houston
page.meta_description: The Riot Comedy Club on Washington Ave: a purpose-built 150-seat room with stand-up seven nights a week, tickets from free to $25. Every show, price, and ticket link, updated daily.
page.description_html:
The Riot Comedy Club is Houston's busiest comedy room, and as of August 2026 it has a permanent home built for the job: a 4,700 square foot venue at 1925 Washington Ave in the Old Sixth Ward, with a custom 150-seat showroom, a daytime coffee shop and cafe, a full evening bar, and full ADA accessibility. It sits next door to Julep, the James Beard Award winning cocktail bar, which makes the block an easy night out before you even buy a ticket.

The club spent years upstairs at Rudyard's in Montrose and outgrew it. Founder Brian Gendron put the reason for moving plainly: as the club grew, it needed a space that fully delivered the experience it wanted to give guests, comedians and staff. The new room is the result, and it is purpose-built rather than borrowed, which is still rare in Houston comedy.

Seven nights a week, and what that actually means

The Riot runs shows every night of the week, usually at 7pm and 9pm, which is more comedy than any other room in the city puts on. Tickets are mostly in the eight to twenty-five dollar range and a meaningful number of the weeknight shows are free. That combination is the whole proposition: you do not have to plan around a headliner's weekend run, because there is a show tonight, and it costs about what a cocktail costs.

The booking leans on tightly curated showcases rather than one comic for ninety minutes. A typical bill is several working comics in a row, often with a touring name carrying credits from Kill Tony, Don't Tell Comedy, or late-night TV. Because the room seats 150, a strong weekend show genuinely does sell out.

The Riot vs. the Improv and Punch Line: which one tonight?

The Houston Improv and Punch Line are the rooms for a name you already know, with the ticket price and the drink minimum that go with it. The Riot is the neighborhood-club answer: cheaper, smaller, no minimum, and open on the nights the big clubs are dark. If you want a specific comic, check the big two. If you want to go see stand-up tonight without a plan, The Riot is usually the answer.

Against the other small rooms, the difference is consistency. The Secret Group is the cheaper, scrappier, more experimental end of the same idea, and The Den is the intimate speakeasy option. The Riot sits between them: a real club with a real showroom, running at a volume nothing else in the city matches.

Know before you go

  • Where: 1925 Washington Ave, Houston, TX 77007, in the Old Sixth Ward, next door to Julep.
  • Show nights: seven nights a week, with evening shows typically at 7pm and 9pm.
  • The room: a custom 150-seat showroom, purpose-built for comedy, fully ADA accessible.
  • Food and drink: a coffee shop and cafe during the day, a full bar and food service in the evening.
  • Parking: ample parking at the new location, a clear upgrade on the old Montrose room. Full breakdown in our Houston comedy club parking guide.
  • Tickets: sold through the club's own site. Weekend shows sell out at 150 seats, so book ahead.
  • Also in Conroe: The Riot runs a second room north of Houston. See The Riot Comedy Club in Conroe.
  • Follow the club: theriothtx.com and @theriothtx.

Every Riot show appears in the listings below automatically, updated twice a day, alongside every other comedy show in Houston. If it is on sale, it is here.

page.title: The Riot Comedy Club (Conroe) — Shows, Tickets & Info
page.meta_title: The Riot Comedy Club Conroe — Shows, Tickets & Info | Comedy Houston
page.meta_description: The Riot Comedy Club's Conroe room inside GuadalaHARRY's: touring headliner stand-up Thursday to Saturday north of Houston, with dinner in the same room. Every show, price, and ticket link.
page.description_html:
The Riot Comedy Club's Conroe room runs inside GuadalaHARRY's at 219 Simonton St in downtown Conroe, about forty miles up I-45 from Houston. It is the second location of The Riot, booked by the same people who run the Washington Ave club, which means Montgomery County gets the same touring comics without the drive into the city.

Shows run Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights. The format matches the flagship: tightly curated showcases of touring headliners backed by strong Houston-area openers, rather than one comic stretched over a full evening. Because the room is inside a working Tex-Mex bar and grill, dinner and the show are the same trip rather than two stops.

Worth the drive, or worth staying local?

If you are already north of the Beltway, Conroe is the easy answer, and on a Thursday it is very likely the closest live stand-up to you. If you are inside the loop, the honest comparison is that The Riot's Washington Ave room books the same caliber of comic seven nights a week, so the drive north only makes sense if Conroe has a specific name you want to see or you are making a night of downtown Conroe.

The reverse is worth saying too: Conroe audiences have spent years driving to Houston for a real comedy club. This room exists so they do not have to, and it books like it means it.

Know before you go

  • Where: 219 Simonton St, Conroe, TX 77301, inside GuadalaHARRY's in downtown Conroe.
  • Show nights: Thursday, Friday and Saturday.
  • Food and drink: full Tex-Mex menu and bar, since the room is inside the restaurant.
  • Phone: (713) 264-8664.
  • Tickets: sold through the club's own site. Every upcoming date is listed below with prices and direct links.
  • Parking: Where to park and what it actually costs is covered venue by venue in our Houston comedy club parking guide.
  • Follow the club: riotconroe.com and @riotconroe. The Conroe room has its own account, separate from the Houston club.

page.title: The Den Comedy Club — Shows, Tickets & Info
page.meta_title: The Den Comedy Club Houston — Shows, Tickets & Info | Comedy Houston
page.meta_description: The Den Comedy Club: Houston's speakeasy stand-up room inside Wolfsmiths in Lindale Park. Real cocktails, no drink minimum, shows Thursday to Saturday. Every date, price, and ticket link, updated daily.
page.description_html:
The Den Comedy Club is Houston's speakeasy comedy room: a hidden stand-up club tucked above Wolfsmiths, the cafe and cocktail bar at 201 Woodard St in Lindale Park, one neighborhood over from the Heights. There is no sign outside. You walk into Wolfsmiths, look for the white orchids, and slip into a room built with wood accents, soft lighting, and seats close enough that every show feels like a private set.

The club opened in March 2026 and is owned by working Houston comedians Janan Araujo-Siam and Onkar Singh, which shapes everything about it. Lineups are curated showcases of the city's best working comics with touring guests mixed in: the kind of bill a comic books to impress other comics, performed for a crowd that found the room on purpose. The space is small enough that shows regularly sell out on word of mouth alone.

The Den vs. Houston Improv vs. Punch Line: which club for which night?

The Houston Improv is the national-headliner room: names you know from Netflix playing multi-night weekend runs at the Marq*E center on the Katy Freeway, with big-club pricing and the standard two-item minimum. Punch Line Houston is the classic club in the middle: strong touring headliners, 18 and up, two-beverage minimum per person. Both are reliable nights out, and if the goal is seeing someone you already know from TV, that is where they will be.

The Den is the other kind of great night. You may not recognize the names on the lineup yet, and that is the point: this is where Houston's best working comics do their sharpest sets in a room small enough to hear the table next to you lose it. Tickets usually cost less than parking near the big clubs, and the intimacy does the rest. Ask a Houston comic where they would take a date to watch stand-up and The Den comes up more often than any room its size should.

Food and drinks: Wolfsmiths downstairs, and no drink minimum

Because The Den lives upstairs from Wolfsmiths, you get real food and real cocktails with table service during the show: a full menu from the kitchen, drinks built by the house mixologist, plus wine, beer, and non-alcoholic options. And unlike the big clubs, The Den does not lean on a drink minimum. Order because the cocktails are good, not because the fine print says two items. Come early, eat downstairs, then head up for the show.

Know before you go

  • Where: 201 Woodard St, Houston, TX 77009, inside Wolfsmiths in Lindale Park, minutes from the Heights.
  • Finding it: no signage. Enter Wolfsmiths and look for the white orchids.
  • Show nights: Thursday through Saturday, with specials in between.
  • Tickets: sold through Eventbrite; every upcoming date is listed below with prices and direct links.
  • Parking: Where to park and what it actually costs is covered venue by venue in our Houston comedy club parking guide.
  • Follow the club: thedencomedyclub.com and @thedencomedyclub.

Every show at The Den appears in the listings below automatically, updated twice a day, alongside every other comedy show in Houston. If it is on sale, it is here.
